newsitem.title: UK: British managers' pay rises seen stable - report.
newsitem.headline: British managers' pay rises seen stable - report.

text.p: British managers' pay increased by an average of 3.4 percent over the last 12 months, marking a notable level of stability, according to a survey on Thursday.

The Reward Group said the increase was in line with pay rises for clerical and operative workers which averaged 3.3 and 3.1 percent over the same period, and recent low settlements suggested management salaries would remain at current levels for some time.
"This period of stability in pay increases is virtually unheard of in recent memory," said Reward Group Managing Director Steve Flather.
But the report said managers' pay could rise by 3.6 percent if Headline inflation, one of the main drivers of pay increases, were to rise from the 2.8 percent it averaged over the last 12 months.
